cues.en: Ladies and gentlemen, please welcome event director of the Game Developers Conference, Megan Scavio. And welcome to the Game Developers Conference. The gentleman about to take the stage to present this morning's keynote doesn't really need much of an introduction. As the creator of some of the greatest games ever made, from railroad tycoons through pirates to the Civilization series, he has already taken his place on the list of legendary game design icons.
cues.zh: 女士们先生们，请欢迎游戏开发者大会的活动总监Megan Scavio。欢迎来到游戏开发者大会。即将登台发表今早主题演讲的这位先生其实不需要太多介绍。作为史上一些最伟大游戏的创作者，从铁路大亨到海盗，再到《文明》系列，他已经跻身传奇游戏设计偶像之列。

cues.en: And he's not done yet. So please join me in welcoming the director of creative development at Firaxis and the father of computer gaming, Mr. Sid Meier. Thank you. Thank you very much. It's great to be here. The title of this talk is the psychology of game design. Everything you know is wrong.
cues.zh: 而他还没停下脚步。所以请和我一起欢迎Firaxis创意开发总监、电脑游戏之父Sid Meier先生。谢谢。非常感谢。很高兴来到这里。这次演讲的题目是游戏设计心理学。你所知道的一切都是错的。

cues.en: I was going to call it, you know, people are funny, gamers are goofy, it's all in your head, or everything you know is questionable. But I thought everything you know is wrong, kind of get the juices flowing, maybe get a little more interaction. The premise of this talk is that, is there any way to get the slides up in the back of the hall? Is that game play
cues.zh: 我本来想叫它，你知道的，人很有趣，玩家很搞笑，一切都在你脑子里，或者你所知道的一切都值得怀疑。但我觉得“你所知道的一切都是错的”更能让人热血沸腾，也许能多点互动。这次演讲的前提是，有没有办法把幻灯片放到大厅后面？那是游戏玩法吗

cues.en: game design is a psychological experience. Gameplay is a psychological experience. When I design a game, a lot of my games are based on historical topics, the history of civilization, railroads, pirates, and the way I would generally approach those topics is, you know, make it realistic, make it true, make it about, you know, the more historical I can make the game, the better it would be, the more
cues.zh: 游戏设计是一种心理体验。玩法是一种心理体验。当我设计游戏时，我的很多游戏都基于历史题材，文明史、铁路、海盗，而我通常处理这些题材的方式是，你知道的，让它真实，让它符合事实，让它关于，你知道的，我越能把游戏做得有历史感，它就越好，越

cues.en: the game is, the better. The more piratey it is, the better. And what I found in taking that approach was that a lot of what I thought I knew was wrong. And the reason was because I really hadn't taken into account what really happens in the player's head. And once that became an important part of kind of my design process, things started to become a lot clearer.
cues.zh: 游戏就越好。越有海盗味就越好。而我发现，采取这种方法后，很多我以为我知道的东西都是错的。原因是我真的没有考虑到玩家脑子里真正发生的事。一旦这成为我设计过程中重要的一部分，事情就开始变得清楚多了。

cues.en: The premise here is that by acknowledging that the gameplay is really a psychological experience, we can save ourselves a lot of time in certain areas. It makes certain parts of the process easier, certain makes other parts of the process more difficult. But at the end of the day, I think we end up with a better game. In the process, as we kind of explore this idea, we're going to kind of run into a few psychological concepts.
cues.zh: 这里的前提是，承认游戏玩法本质上是一种心理体验，我们就能在某些方面省下大量时间。它让流程中的某些部分变简单，也让另一些部分变难。但归根结底，我认为最终会得到一款更好的游戏。在这个过程中，当我们探索这个想法时，会遇到一些心理学概念。

cues.en: egomaniac. So one of them we'll have to explore. Basically if you play civilization, you are an egomaniac. I mean, it says right on the box, you know, build a civilization to stand the test of time. And you're there like, oh, yeah, I can do that. I can do that. So you are an egomaniac, okay. We'll also be looking into paranoia, delusion, and
cues.zh: 自大狂。其中一个我们就得探讨一下。基本上，如果你玩《文明》，你就是个自大狂。我是说，盒子上就写着，建立一个经受时间考验的文明。你坐在那儿就想，哦对，我能做到。我能做到。所以你就是个自大狂，好吧。我们还会研究偏执、妄想，以及

cues.en: self-destructive behavior. This is ways that players actually kind of make the game less fun for themselves. Things they do to kind of detract from the fun of the game and ways that as a designer we can try and minimize those, preempt those and try and prevent that from happening. So those are some of the things we'll be looking at in the course of this talk. So the first area where psychology really kind of plays an important role in game design.
cues.zh: 自我毁灭行为。这就是玩家实际上让自己玩得没那么开心的方式。他们做一些削弱游戏乐趣的事，而作为设计师，我们要设法尽量减少这些、预先防范，并阻止其发生。这些就是本次演讲中我们会探讨的部分内容。那么，心理学在游戏设计中真正发挥重要作用的第一个领域，

cues.en: something I call the winner paradox. In real life, we don't always win. There are, what, 28 teams in the National Football League, and only one of them gets to win the Super Bowl. There are 25 teams in the NBA. You know, they all go to the playoffs, I guess. But at the end of the day, there's only one team that gets to hold the golden trophy of NBA
cues.zh: 是我称之为赢家悖论的东西。在现实生活中，我们并不总能赢。国家橄榄球联盟有28支球队，只有一支能赢得超级碗。NBA有25支球队。你知道，他们大概都能进季后赛。但归根结底，只有一支球队能捧起NBA的金色奖杯

cues.en: whatever that is. So in the real world, you don't always win. However, in the world of games, you pretty much always win. And the psychological phenomenon is that the player doesn't really complain about that, doesn't object. That's not a problem. I don't get letters saying, you know, dear Sid, I loved your game, but I won way too much.
cues.zh: 管那是什么。所以在现实世界里，你并不总能赢。然而，在游戏世界里，你几乎总能赢。而这一心理现象是，玩家并不会真的抱怨这一点，不会反对。那不是问题。我不会收到信说，亲爱的Sid，我很喜欢你的游戏，但我赢太多了。

cues.en: And this is actually true of other forms of entertainment. You know, Rambo, you know, at the end of the movie he's going to come out all right. Sherlock Holmes always solves the mystery by the end of the chapter. So I think this is kind of fundamental to entertainment, but it's certainly something that we're aware of in designing video games, that the player
cues.zh: 这对其他娱乐形式也同样适用。你知道，兰博，在电影结尾他总会平安无事。福尔摩斯总能在章节结束前解开谜团。所以我认为这算是娱乐的根本，但在设计电子游戏时我们当然会意识到这一点，那就是玩家

cues.en: the player's looking for a satisfactory conclusion. That might not always include winning, but very often it does. And this idea of kind of a satisfactory conclusion to the game, I think, is something to really keep in mind in the design process. Some of the tools that we have at our disposal to create this journey for the player through the game, reward and punishment. In other words, good things happening to the player, not so good things happening to the player.
cues.zh: 玩家在寻求一个满意的结局。这未必总是包含获胜，但很多时候确实如此。这种给游戏一个满意结局的想法，我觉得在设计过程中真的要牢记在心。我们可用来为玩家打造这段游戏旅程的一些工具，就是奖励与惩罚。换句话说，好事发生在玩家身上，不太好的事也发生在玩家身上。

cues.en: There's an interesting dichotomy in how these are deployed in games. When you reward the player, you know, you discovered this cool place on the map, here's 100 gold. The player, you know, gladly accepts that, doesn't question, did I really earn that? Do I deserve that? Players are very much inclined to
cues.zh: 这些在游戏中的运用存在一种有趣的对立。当你奖励玩家时，比如你发现了地图上这个很酷的地方，给你100金币。玩家会欣然接受，不会质疑，我真的挣到了吗？我配得上吗？玩家非常倾向于

cues.en: to accept anything you give them gladly and feel it was their own clever play, their own incredible strategy that earned them that cool reward. On the other hand, if something bad happens to the player, your game is broken, there's something horribly wrong, the game is cheating. It's really important to be very careful with the setbacks that the player experiences in the game. It's important that the player understand why those things happened.
cues.zh: 欣然接受你给予的一切，并觉得那是自己聪明的玩法、自己惊人的策略才赢得了那个酷炫的奖励。另一方面，如果坏事发生在玩家身上，那就是你的游戏有bug，出了严重问题，游戏在作弊。对玩家在游戏中经历的挫折要非常小心，这真的很重要。重要的是让玩家理解这些事情为什么会发生。

cues.en: and especially how to prevent that from happening the next time. And anytime you can kind of plant that seed of the next time in the player's head, you're well on your way to this idea of replayability, that the player's going to play again. Next time I'm going to try something different, maybe that might not happen. So a big part of the value of these games is in their replayability. So any opportunity that you have to plant the seed of replayability, I think, is important.
cues.zh: 尤其是如何防止下次再发生。只要你能在玩家脑中埋下“下次”的种子，你就已经踏上了可重玩性这条路，玩家会再玩一次。“下次我要试试别的，也许就不会这样了。”所以这类游戏的价值很大一部分在于可重玩性。因此，任何能埋下可重玩性种子的机会，我认为都很重要。

cues.en: And by really carefully handling the idea of punishment and setbacks where you explain why it happened and how it can be branded the next time, that's very important. In terms of rewards, another key thing that we think about is the first 15 minutes. One of our rules of game design is that the first 15 minutes have to be really compelling, really fun, kind of almost a foreshadowing of all the cool stuff that's going to happen later in the game.
cues.zh: 通过非常谨慎地处理惩罚和挫折，解释为什么会发生、下次如何改进，这非常重要。在奖励方面，我们考虑的另一个关键点是前15分钟。我们的游戏设计规则之一是，前15分钟必须非常引人入胜、非常有趣，几乎要预示游戏后期所有精彩内容。

cues.en: And these rewards are really a way of making the player feel comfortable in this world. Letting them know that they're on the right track. They're on their way. Cool stuff is happening and even cooler stuff is going to be happening later on. And these early rewards, you can almost not reward the player enough in the very early stages of the game to kind of get them invested, get them committed, get them to be part of the world that you're creating.
cues.zh: 这些奖励其实是让玩家在这个世界里感到自在的一种方式。让他们知道自己走在正轨上、正在前进，精彩的事情正在发生，更精彩的事情还在后头。而在游戏早期阶段，这些早期奖励几乎怎么给都不为过，目的是让玩家投入进来、承诺下来，成为你所创造的世界的一部分。

cues.en: Now, this doesn't negate the value of difficulty levels. I'm not advocating an elastic difficulty that kind of always pushes the player forward and never provides any challenges. A number of years ago, I gave a talk on difficulty levels and it was very convincingly
cues.zh: 当然，这并不否定难度等级的价值。我并不是在提倡一种弹性难度，总是把玩家往前推，从不提供任何挑战。几年前，我做过一个关于难度等级的演讲，非常有说服力地

cues.en: made the point that four difficulty levels were the perfect number of difficulty levels. There needed to be one for introducing the player of the game where the player could basically always win, one for the casual player, one for the player who's really experienced, and then the fourth difficulty level, which would be the ultimate challenge. I was wrong about that. Apparently we need nine difficulty levels. The latest Civilization IV has nine difficulty levels.
cues.zh: 说明了四个难度等级是完美的难度等级数量。需要有一个用来引导玩家入门的等级，玩家基本上总能赢；一个面向休闲玩家的等级；一个面向真正经验丰富的玩家的等级；然后是第四个难度等级，也就是终极挑战。我那时错了。显然我们需要九个难度等级。《文明IV》最新版本就有九个难度等级。

cues.en: And it really points out how this idea of progress and advancement is so rewarding for the player. The reason we have these difficulty levels is to give the player this feeling that there's always another challenge out there, that they've mastered this level, they're ready to move on to the next level. And that's another reward is this idea of getting to the next level in the game. So you want your player to feel that they are above average. They're doing well.
cues.zh: 这确实说明了进步和提升这个理念对玩家来说是多么有回报感。我们设置这些难度等级的原因，是给玩家一种感觉：总还有另一个挑战在等着他们，他们已经掌握了这个等级，准备好进入下一个等级了。而进入游戏的下一个等级这种想法，本身就是另一种奖励。所以你想让玩家觉得自己高于平均水平，觉得自己做得很好。

cues.en: And they're going to do even better as they go deeper into the game. I think that, again, if you kind of follow the first 15-minute rule, it's very important that you kind of start the player off with a very positive experience. The unholy alliance. This is a concept that I want to trademark. I think this is a really cool idea. I missed out on the uncanny valley. And I never trademarked interesting decisions. But unholy alliance, I think, is a
cues.zh: 而且随着他们深入游戏，他们会做得更好。我认为，再次强调，如果你遵循最初的15分钟规则，那么让玩家一开始就获得非常积极的体验是非常重要的。不神圣的同盟。这是一个我想注册商标的概念。我觉得这是个很酷的想法。我错过了恐怖谷。我也一直没给有趣决策注册商标。但不神圣的同盟，我认为是一个

cues.en: It's a concept that in many ways defines the relationship between the player and the designer. The unholy alliance is an agreement that the player and the designer make with each other. I'm gonna pretend certain things, you're gonna pretend certain things and together we'll have a great experience. So one of the things that we pretend as designers
cues.zh: 这个概念在很多方面定义了玩家和设计师之间的关系。不神圣的同盟是玩家和设计师彼此达成的一项协议。我会假装某些事情，你会假装某些事情，然后我们一起获得很棒的体验。所以作为设计师，我们假装的其中一件事

cues.en: is that the player is good. You're really good. That's kind of a mantra from us. That we want the player to feel good about the play experience and themselves as they're playing. And one example, perhaps where this kind of went off the tracks is in the history of flight simulators going back a number of years. Early on they were kind of easy to play.
cues.zh: 就是玩家很厉害。你真的很厉害。这算是我们的口头禅。我们希望玩家在对游戏体验和自己在游戏中的表现感觉良好。也许有一个例子偏离了正轨，那就是飞行模拟器的历史，可以追溯到很多年前。早期它们玩起来还算简单。

cues.en: very accessible, you shoot down a lot of planes, you'd have a lot of fun. And then we got to where every succeeding iteration of flight simulators became a little more realistic, a little more complex, a little more of a simulation. And pretty soon the player went from I'm good to I'm not good. I'm confused. My plane is on fire and I'm falling out of the sky.
cues.zh: 非常容易上手，你能击落很多飞机，会玩得很开心。后来每一代飞行模拟器都变得更真实、更复杂、更像模拟。很快玩家就从“我很厉害”变成了“我不行，我糊涂了，我的飞机着火了，我从天上掉下来了”。

cues.en: And the fun kind of went out of them. And I think we have to be aware of this phenomenon that it's all about the player. The player is the star of the game. Their experience is what's key, what's critical. And keeping them feeling good about themselves is certainly an important part of the experience that we provide for them. Another part of this unholy alliance is the player's role.
cues.zh: 乐趣就没了。我觉得我们必须意识到这个现象：一切都围绕玩家。玩家是游戏的主角。他们的体验才是关键、才是核心。让他们对自己感觉良好，当然是我们提供体验的重要部分。这种“不神圣联盟”的另一部分，是玩家的角色。

cues.en: The player really needs to be willing to suspend their disbelief. They need to inhabit that character. They need to take on that role that you're providing them, whether it's a king of a great civilization or managing a railroad or being a cool pirate. The player has to be willing to suspend their disbelief. They're part of the bargain.
cues.zh: 玩家真的需要愿意暂时放下怀疑。他们需要融入那个角色，接受你给他们的身份，不管是伟大文明的国王、管理铁路，还是当个酷海盗。玩家必须愿意放下怀疑。这是交易的一部分。

cues.en: When we go to a movie, my wife asked her after we've seen a movie, you know, how did you like the movie? A lot of times she'll say, well, you know, I came out of that movie twice or I never got into that movie or I never came out of the movie. Very aware of the value of suspending your disbelief to enjoy the experience or to make it more compelling. So part of our job is to help the player to suspend their disbelief. And I think in some ways,
cues.zh: 我们去看电影，看完后我妻子会问，你觉得电影怎么样？她经常说，我看的时候出戏了两次，或者我根本没入戏，或者我一直没从电影里出来。她很在意“放下怀疑”对享受体验、让体验更吸引人的价值。所以我们的部分工作，就是帮玩家放下怀疑。我觉得在某些方面，

cues.en: those of us that are old time designers have a little bit of an advantage there in that we worked in the good old days of 16 color graphics and things like that where we really had to work hard to get the player to believe that what was happening on the screen was the management of a great empire or building a railroad system or things like that. So I think having that experience was helpful in really understanding
cues.zh: 我们这些老派设计师还有点优势，因为我们经历过16色图形的美好旧时光，那时候真得努力让玩家相信屏幕上发生的是管理伟大帝国或修建铁路系统之类的事。所以我觉得那种经历很有帮助，让人真正理解

cues.en: some of the challenges of getting the player to suspend their disbelief. One of the other agreements that we make, I think, in this unholy alliance with the player is the idea of moral clarity. And let me give you an example. Here's a screenshot from a civilization revolution where we're negotiating with the great Genghis Khan.
cues.zh: 让玩家放下怀疑的一些挑战。我觉得在这种与玩家的“不神圣联盟”里，另一个约定是道德清晰感。我举个例子。这是《文明革命》的截图，我们正在和伟大的成吉思汗谈判。

cues.en: And one of the comments that I got back from play testers was, these leaders are very kind of cranky and aggressive. I might be winning the battle against them. They might be down to their last city. And they're still kind of up there saying, hey, you'll never take me down. I'm the greatest civilization of all time. Come on, attack me. I dare you. And they said, well, that just doesn't seem right. They shouldn't have the attitude if I'm winning.
cues.zh: 我从试玩者那里收到的一条反馈是，这些领袖太暴躁、太有攻击性了。我可能眼看就要打赢他们了，他们可能只剩最后一座城，却还在那儿嘴硬：“嘿，你永远打不倒我。我是史上最伟大的文明。来啊，打我啊，你敢吗？”他们说，这感觉不对劲。我都要赢了，他们不该还这态度。

cues.en: And my question was, well, you know, what would you like them to say? Do you want them to say, oh, you know, please don't hurt me. We have only one city left and there's women and children there and, you know, please leave me alone. To me, that's like a moral dilemma, you know. I mean, I want to win. I want to capture their city. It's Genghis Khan, for goodness sake. But I'm faced with a moral dilemma.
cues.zh: 我就问，那你们希望他们说什么？希望他们说：“哦，求你别伤害我。我们只剩一座城了，里面还有妇女和孩子，求你别管我了”？对我来说，这就是道德困境。我是说，我想赢，我想攻下他们的城。拜托，这可是成吉思汗。但我面临道德困境。

cues.en: I think it's more satisfying, and that's something we discovered, it's more satisfying to win against bad Genghis, cranky Genghis, than it is if, you know, there was some kind of a moral cloud over the actions that you were taking. MAD is a concept called Mutually Assured Destruction. How many of you remember the Cold War?
cues.zh: 我觉得这样更有满足感——这是我们发现的——打败那个凶巴巴的坏成吉思汗，比你在行动时还背着某种道德包袱要有满足感得多。MAD 是一个概念，叫“相互确保摧毁”。你们有多少人还记得冷战？

cues.en: Let's hear it for the Cold War. Okay. The idea of mutually assured destruction was that, you know, we had all these nuclear weapons and the Russians had all these nuclear weapons and we could just blow each other up any time we wanted to. But the reason we didn't, because we knew the other side had all these nuclear weapons. And there's an amazing parallel to that in the relationship between game designers and the player.
cues.zh: 为冷战鼓个掌吧。好。“相互确保摧毁”的理念是，我们有那么多核武器，俄罗斯人也有那么多核武器，我们随时都能把彼此炸上天。但我们没这么做的原因，是我们知道对方也有那么多核武器。而游戏设计者和玩家之间的关系，与这有着惊人的相似之处。

cues.en: the player can actually destroy the experience at any time they want to. They can quit the game. They can play in a way, in a different way. They can sheath. They can do all sorts of stuff to kind of destroy the experience. And as a game designer, we can mess up the game as well. We can kind of lose the thread of the fantasy. There was a game that we were working on at MicroProse many years ago that kind of illustrated this to me. It was an adventure game and basically
cues.zh: 玩家其实随时都能毁掉这种体验。他们可以退出游戏。他们可以换一种玩法。他们可以作弊。他们可以做各种事情来破坏体验。而作为游戏设计师，我们也可能把游戏搞砸。我们可能会让幻想失去连贯性。很多年前我们在 MicroProse 做的一款游戏，就让我明白了这一点。那是一款冒险游戏，基本上

cues.en: You kind of started at the beginning of the road and you adventured your way on down until you got to the castle and finally got to see the king and had gone through this great adventure. And when you got to the king, all of a sudden it was revealed to you that the king who you thought was a good guy or actually a bad guy and everything was turned around and you had to go back down the path. You just come back to the beginning to do the real thing that you were supposed to do in the first place.
cues.zh: 你大概从路的起点出发，一路冒险前行，直到抵达城堡，终于见到国王，走完了这场伟大的冒险。可当你见到国王时，突然发现你原以为是好人的国王其实是坏人，一切都被反转，你不得不沿路返回。你刚回到起点，去做你一开始就该做的真正任务。

cues.en: To me, that was us messing up the game. Basically, I can imagine the design meetings, imagine the look on the player's face when they realize that all this work they've done has to be in vain, and the surprise, and the amazing design. They'll think, what an amazing design to surprise me. I said, no, that's not what they're going to think. I think I just wasted eight hours on this stupid game.
cues.zh: 对我来说，那就是我们把游戏搞砸了。基本上，我能想象设计会议上的情形，想象玩家意识到自己做的所有这些努力都白费时的表情，还有那种惊讶，以及所谓“绝妙设计”。他们会想：多妙的设计啊，居然能给我这种惊喜。我说，不，他们不会这么想。他们会想：我刚刚在这破游戏上浪费了八个小时。

cues.en: At that point they would mutually assuredly destruct the game, I believe. So there are ways, I think, again, that we need to be careful that we're true to the story of the game and value the player's time. Another part of this alliance I think that we make with players is in the area of style. Things that convey
cues.zh: 到那时，我相信游戏必定会自我毁灭。所以，我认为我们需要谨慎行事，确保忠实于游戏的故事，并重视玩家的时间。我认为我们与玩家之间的这种联盟的另一个方面在于风格。那些能传达

cues.en: what the spirit of your game is. If you start the game off and have kind of a lighthearted music, atmosphere, cartoony graphics, and all of a sudden people's heads start exploding, then you haven't lived up to the alliance. You're not giving the player what you promised them. On the other hand, if you
cues.zh: 你游戏精神的东西。如果你开始游戏时，有轻松愉快的音乐、氛围和卡通化的画面，然后突然间人们的头开始爆炸，那你就没有履行这个联盟。你没有给玩家你所承诺的东西。另一方面，如果你

cues.en: If you have dark foreboding sound in music and it ends up being a very simple game, again, you kind of are fooling the player. And if I'm playing a game that starts off light and happy and cartoony, all of a sudden terrible things start to happen. That's when the player loses their suspension of disbelief and turns off their game and moves on.
cues.zh: 如果你的音乐中有阴暗不祥的声音，而结果却是一个非常简单的游戏，那么你又有点在欺骗玩家。如果我正在玩一个开始时轻松愉快、卡通化的游戏，突然间可怕的事情开始发生，这时玩家就会失去对虚构的信任，关掉游戏，继续前行。

cues.en: The only way to kind of maintain the suspension of disbelief, which is critical to keeping the player in the game, is to really make that a priority and use things like humor style, music, atmosphere, all these tools to be consistent and keep the player in your world. So probably where it became most clear to me that
cues.zh: 维持对虚构的信任——这对留住玩家至关重要——的唯一方法就是真正将其作为优先事项，并利用幽默风格、音乐、氛围等所有工具来保持一致性，让玩家留在你的世界里。所以，对我来说，最明显的地方可能是

cues.en: player psychology has absolutely nothing to do with rational thought was in the process of putting together the battle system in civilization and revolution. My background is in mathematics and science and programming and I think of myself as a logical person. And what we did in revolution was we would show you before a battle what the odds were. In this example, our attacker here has a 1.5.
cues.zh: 玩家心理与理性思考完全无关，这一点在我构建《文明：革命》的战斗系统时变得尤为明显。我的背景是数学、科学和编程，我认为自己是一个逻辑性强的人。而在《革命》中，我们所做的是在战斗前向你展示胜算。在这个例子中，我们的攻击者这里有1.5的胜算。

cues.en: And the defender, the barbarians have a 0.5. They would have a 1. The barbarians are basically 1. But since they're uncivilized, they take a 50% penalty for that. So they're only 0.5. And part of the fun of being a designer is kind of throwing those little things into the game, you know, uncivilized, minus 50%. Take that. So in this case,
cues.zh: 而防守方呢，野蛮人是0.5。他们本该是1。野蛮人基础就是1。但因为他们未开化，所以要承受50%的惩罚。所以就只有0.5了。作为设计师，乐趣之一就是把这种小细节塞进游戏里，比如，未开化，减50%。就这么着。所以在这个例子里，

cues.en: As a mathematician, this would be a three to one battle. 1.5 to 2.5. Three to one, the attacker should win three times, the defender should win one time out of four. Very clear, very simple. That's what mathematics says. That's the way it should work. That's not the way our players saw it. Basically, at a certain point, players feel they are going to win the battle.
cues.zh: 作为数学家，这会是一场三对一的战斗。1.5对2.5。三对一，攻方应该赢三次，守方四次里赢一次。非常清楚，非常简单。数学就是这么说的。本该如此运作。但玩家的看法可不是这样。基本上，到了某个节点，玩家会觉得自己就要赢了。

cues.en: And they would come to me and say, you know, I had this battle. It was three to one. I lost. I was like, well, yeah, you know, three to one. You're going to lose every once in a while. No, no, you don't understand. It was three to one. Three. Three is big. One is small. I had the big number. You know, shouldn't I have one? So I realized, okay, there's something going on here.
cues.zh: 然后他们会来找我说，你知道吗，我打了这场仗，三对一，我输了。我就说，嗯，是啊，三对一嘛，你偶尔也会输一次。不，不，你不明白，是三对一。三，三很大，一小。我拿的是大数字，我不该赢一次吗？于是我意识到，好吧，这里面有点问题。

cues.en: So we adjusted our system by actually breaking the battle up into kind of more atomic little battles to make the results come out more than the player expected. And then I watched some more players playing, and this time the player had won against three. The player had won, the little tiny one, and the AI had the big gigantic three. And I watched, and lo and behold, the player won the battle. And I said,
cues.zh: 所以我们调整了系统，把战斗拆分成更原子化的小战斗，让结果更符合玩家的预期。然后我又观察了一些玩家对战，这次玩家以少胜多，打败了三个。玩家赢了，那个小小的一，而AI拿的是巨大的三。我看着，果不其然，玩家赢了这场战斗。我说，

cues.en: Doesn't that feel wrong to you? That you with your little tiny one, one against the huge three?" And they said, no. Doesn't feel wrong at all. I had, you know, clever tactics and strategy, clean living. It all adds up to me winning. So we realized that something was going on there psychologically that isn't exactly mathematics. I'm not sure what it is, but it's not mathematics.
cues.zh: “你不觉得这不对劲吗？你那个小小的一，一对上巨大的三？”他们说，不，一点都不觉得不对劲。我有巧妙的战术和策略，生活检点，这些都让我赢了。所以我们意识到，这里面有某种心理层面的东西，不完全是数学。我不确定那是什么，但肯定不是数学。

cues.en: we made a few adjustments and said, okay, now are you happy with the way combat works? And we found that there is this point, and it's kind of around three to one, four to one, where people do expect to pretty much win every time. So, okay. We said, okay, that's fine. We can live with that. Anything else? You know? They said, well, there's just one little thing. I'm okay, you know,
cues.zh: 我们做了一些调整，然后说，好，现在你对战斗机制满意了吗？我们发现有一个临界点，大约在3比1、4比1左右，人们确实期望几乎每次都能赢。所以，好吧。我们说，行，这没问题。我们可以接受。还有别的吗？你知道吗？他们说，嗯，就一个小问题。我说，好吧，你知道，

cues.en: here's a two to one battle. Are you okay with winning most of the time but every now and then losing a two to one? The player said, yeah, yeah, yeah, you know, two to one. I'm okay with that. Two to one. I should win most of the time but every now and then I can lose. So, okay, good. So what's your problem? Well, I had this 20 to 10 battle and I lost. It was 20 to 10. I said, yeah. 20 to 10. I had 10 more.
cues.zh: 这里是一场2比1的战斗。你接受大多数时候赢，但偶尔输掉一场2比1的战斗吗？玩家说，对对对，你知道，2比1嘛。我可以接受。2比1，我应该大多数时候赢，但偶尔也可以输。所以，好，没问题。那你的问题是什么？嗯，我打了一场20对10的战斗，我输了。是20对10。我说，是啊。20对10。我多了10个。

cues.en: than the 10. I had 20. But it's that, I said, you know, it's not 2 to 1. No. It's 20 to 10. That's a whole different odds than 2 to 1. Okay. So we actually adjusted, you know, okay. I can see you have 10 more. So that's a lot. Okay. Cool. Okay. So now, you know, maybe just give the game back. Now are you happy?
cues.zh: 比那10个多。我有20个。但问题在于，我说，你知道，这不是2比1。不，这是20比10。这跟2比1是完全不同的赔率。好吧。所以我们实际上做了调整，你知道，好吧。我明白你多了10个。这确实很多。好，酷。好。那么现在，你知道，也许把游戏还给我吧。现在你满意了吗？

cues.en: Well, kind of. But let me tell you what happened. I had this two-to-one battle and I lost, which is okay. We've had this discussion, I understand now, but every now and then I'm going to lose a two-to-one battle. But right after that, I had another two-to-one battle and I lost again. How can that be? How can I lose two two-to-one battles? I mean, one I can understand. The computers have to get me, obviously.
cues.zh: 嗯，差不多吧。但让我告诉你发生了什么。我打了一场2比1的战斗，我输了，这没关系。我们讨论过这个，我现在理解了，但偶尔我会输掉一场2比1的战斗。但紧接着，我又打了一场2比1的战斗，又输了。这怎么可能？我怎么能连输两场2比1的战斗？我是说，输一场我能理解。电脑总得赢我一次，显然。

cues.en: We actually take into account the results of previous battles. Now when we do our combat calculations. And then the player was very happy. And we don't really do this just to make the player happy. But it's really when something happens in a battle like this that feels wrong, we start to lose that suspension of disbelief. The player comes out of the game.
cues.zh: 我们实际上会考虑之前战斗的结果。现在进行战斗计算时，玩家非常开心。我们这样做并不只是为了取悦玩家。而是当战斗中出现让人感觉不对劲的情况时，我们就会开始失去那种悬置怀疑感。玩家会从游戏中抽离出来。

cues.en: and starts to pay attention to other things that are going on and not what's in the game. So it's all part of the process of really trying to maintain the suspension of disbelief as the player is playing the game. And something really kind of clear and instructive about this process. I think the interaction between logic and science and math and psychology kind of really became clear to me in this process. And I think it all makes sense, but it's
cues.zh: 开始关注周围发生的其他事情，而不是游戏里的内容。所以这都是为了在玩家玩游戏时尽量维持悬置怀疑感的过程的一部分。这个过程有一些非常清晰且有启发性的事情。我觉得逻辑、科学、数学和心理学之间的互动在这个过程中变得非常清晰。我认为这一切都说得通，但它

cues.en: It's very counterintuitive. And I think one of the things about really including the psychological part of things in game thinking and design is it's going to run into a number of counterintuitive things. And we'll see a little more of that later. But there are many times where that actually can work to your advantage. And it's not always quite the process that we just went through. So this part is called My Bad.
cues.zh: 非常反直觉。我认为在游戏思维和设计中真正纳入心理学因素，会遇到许多反直觉的事情。我们稍后会看到更多。但很多时候这实际上能对你有利。而且并不总是我们刚刚经历的那个过程。所以这部分叫做“我的错”。

cues.en: times when I really screwed up and kind of came to realize that it was because my brain was too logical and scientific and I hadn't really included a lot of the psychological aspects of what goes on in games. The first bad, bad thing I did in life was to make Civilization a real-time game, the original prototype of Civilization.
cues.zh: 那些我真的搞砸了的时刻，我意识到那是因为我的大脑太逻辑化、太科学化，我没有真正纳入游戏中发生的许多心理层面。我人生中第一个糟糕的错误，是把《文明》做成了实时游戏，即《文明》的原始原型。

cues.en: was real-time, kind of inspired by SimCity and that genre of games where you're kind of watching something grow. SimCity, I think, inspired a lot of designers to branch out in kind of construction, oriented games, growth games. But what we found with the real-time version of Civilization was that the player really became an observer.
cues.zh: 实时制，灵感来自《模拟城市》那类游戏，就是看着某个东西慢慢成长。我觉得《模拟城市》启发了很多设计师，去做建造类、成长类的游戏。但我们发现，《文明》的实时版本里，玩家真的变成了一个旁观者。

cues.en: was watching what's going on, was really just an observer. And the mantra that we had in mind for Civilization was, it's good to be king. And we found that when we made it a turn-based game, all of a sudden, lights went off. All of a sudden, the player was no longer an observer. They were the star of the game. They were the key ingredient, and they made things happen.
cues.zh: 只是看着发生的一切，纯粹就是个观察者。而我们做《文明》时的信条是：当国王的感觉真好。后来我们发现，一旦改成回合制，突然间，灯就亮了。突然间，玩家不再是旁观者。他们成了游戏的主角。他们成了关键要素，是他们推动了事情发生。

cues.en: kind of ironic since CIV is now the poster child for turn-based gaming. But CIV actually started off as a real-time game. And that was my bad. Sorry about that. Another bad thing that I did in the original civilization design was to include this idea of rise and fall. Wouldn't it be cool if you built this cool civilization?
cues.zh: 说来有点讽刺，因为《文明》现在成了回合制游戏的标杆。但《文明》最初其实是个实时制游戏。那是我的锅。抱歉。我在初代《文明》设计里干的另一件坏事，是加入了兴衰这个设定。你想啊，如果你建起了一个很酷的文明，

cues.en: And then, you know, you had this kind of setback and it started to crumble, you know, and just before it disappeared, you rescued it and you came back to win even more strong and powerfully than you did before. You know, wouldn't that be an awesome experience? No. Not really. What we found was that just at the cusp of the crumble, most players would reload a save game. And they would never experience the glorious re-rise that we had
cues.zh: 然后呢，你遭遇了挫折，它开始崩塌，就在它即将消失之前，你把它救了回来，然后卷土重来，比之前更强更猛。你想，那岂不是超棒的体验？不。其实不然。我们发现，就在崩塌的边缘，大多数玩家会读档。他们永远不会经历我们为他们设想的

cues.en: in mind for them. So civilization is basically a game about progress. A game about rise, rise, and more rise. And not so much the fall. Another badness that I perpetrated was in the original civilization tech tree. The idea that I had in mind was that technology would be this interesting path of kind of discovery through the darkness
cues.zh: 那种辉煌的复兴。所以《文明》本质上是个关于进步的游戏。关于崛起、崛起、再崛起的游戏。而不是衰落。我犯下的另一件坏事，是在初代《文明》的科技树里。我当时的想法是，科技应该是一条有趣的、在黑暗中探索发现的路径，

cues.en: and you would never know where the different paths of technology would lead. It seemed to me totally wacky that you would be thinking back in 3000 BC, okay, if I discover iron working, someday I'm going to have gunpowder and nuclear weapons. So we randomized the tech tree. We did a lot of things to make that process kind of mysterious.
cues.zh: 你永远不知道不同的科技路径会通向哪里。在我看来，你在公元前3000年就盘算着，好，如果我发现了铁器加工，将来总有一天我会有火药和核武器，这简直太荒唐了。所以我们把科技树随机化了。我们做了很多事，让这个过程变得有点神秘。

cues.en: But once players realized, you know, generally the second time they played that there was gunpowder out there, their only goal was, you know, how do I get to gunpowder most quickly? You know, give me the road, you know, don't randomize, don't mysteriousize this thing. I know there's gunpowder out there, you know, you can't fool me. And we understood that players want to be in control. They really want to know what's going on. And the kind of broader lesson from this for me
cues.zh: 但一旦玩家意识到，通常是在他们第二次玩的时候，发现外面有火药，他们唯一的目标就变成了：我怎么最快拿到火药？给我一条明路，别随机化，别把这事搞得神秘兮兮的。我知道外面有火药，你骗不了我。我们明白了，玩家想要掌控感。他们真的想知道发生了什么。这给我带来的更广泛的教训

cues.en: was that any kind of randomness really needs to be treated with a lot of care. We also had the idea in the original Civilization of these kind of great natural disasters. Wouldn't it be cool to have a volcano, a crocodile blowing up for the plague and all these kind of famous world events happening in the game, kind of randomly? No, it wouldn't. Again, whenever anything random happens to the player,
cues.zh: 就是任何形式的随机性都需要非常谨慎地对待。我们在最初的《文明》里也有这种大灾难的想法。来个火山、鳄鱼爆炸、瘟疫，以及所有这些著名的世界事件随机在游戏里发生，岂不是很酷？不，一点也不酷。同样，每当玩家遇到随机事件，

cues.en: Paranoia strikes in. Paranoia was one of our early psychological feelings. The player feels that the computer did that, rolled that random number just to make their life more difficult or they were just about to win. So random events have to be treated very, very carefully. Because if they are significant, basically the player will find the worst
cues.zh: 偏执感就会袭来。偏执是我们早期的心理感受之一。玩家会觉得是电脑故意这么做、故意掷出那个随机数，就是为了让他们的日子更难过，或者在他们快要赢的时候捣乱。所以随机事件必须非常非常小心地处理。因为如果这些事件影响重大，基本上玩家会找到最糟糕、

cues.en: and most paranoid explanation for what just happened in the game. Randomness at a low level certainly helps a lot in variety, replayability, things like that, but really need to be careful with randomness at a really significant level. I'm going to skip the co-redaction rule. That's kind of boring. The dino's game was another mistake that I made.
cues.zh: 最偏执的解释来解读游戏里刚发生的事。低层级的随机性确实对多样性、重玩性等方面很有帮助，但在真正重要的层级上，真的需要小心处理随机性。我要跳过共同编辑规则，那个有点无聊。恐龙游戏是我犯的另一个错误。

cues.en: a while back I gave a talk called dinosaurs the three glorious failures. Basically that was a game that I thought would be very cool. Tried to create. Did three different versions. One was a RTS type game. One was more of a strategy game. One was actually a card game. And none of them really kind of gelled together. And I was disappointed. I thought dinosaurs are very cool. And I may be able to make a cool game about this. But it never really
cues.zh: 前阵子我做过一个演讲，叫《恐龙：三次辉煌的失败》。那其实是我觉得会非常酷的一款游戏，我试着做出来，做了三个不同版本。一个是RTS类型的游戏，一个更偏向策略游戏，还有一个其实是卡牌游戏。但它们都没能真正融合成型。我很失望，我觉得恐龙很酷，也许能做出一个很酷的游戏，但它始终

cues.en: came together for reasons I'm not quite sure of yet. But what's interesting to me, though, is that after civilization, that's almost the best known game. When I talk to people, when I run into people, you know, besides civilization, the other question is where is the dino game, you know? So this game that I never made is like the second most interesting game for gamers. So that was my bad, but I'll
cues.zh: 没能成形，原因我自己到现在也不太清楚。但有意思的是，在《文明》之后，那几乎是最有名的游戏了。我跟人聊天、碰到人的时候，除了《文明》，另一个问题就是：恐龙游戏在哪呢？所以这款我从没做出来的游戏，对玩家来说居然成了第二有趣的游戏。这算是我的锅吧，不过

cues.en: is not over yet. And Civilization Network. This is a new game that we're working on. Civilization for the Facebook platform. A lot of kind of fun game concepts that we get to play with here.
cues.zh: 还没结束。还有《文明网络版》。这是我们正在做的一款新游戏，面向Facebook平台的《文明》。这里面有很多好玩的游戏概念可以让我们去发挥。

cues.en: people playing on kind of an interesting schedule, maybe a little bit of time a day, a little more time a day, kind of making the game interesting if you're playing at the same time as other players or if you're playing at different times with other players. The idea that you're playing with friends so that we can really focus a lot on cooperative gameplay, also include competitive gameplay, individual gameplay, all different kinds of gameplay mixed together. So this is really kind of a fun world to take civilization into.
cues.zh: 玩家们的游玩节奏很有意思，可能一天玩一点时间，某天多玩一点，如果你和其他玩家同时在线玩，或者在不同时间和其他玩家玩，游戏都会变得很有趣。你在和朋友一起玩，所以我们可以真正大量聚焦合作玩法，同时也包含竞争玩法、单人玩法，各种不同的玩法混合在一起。所以把《文明》带进这样一个世界，真的很好玩。

cues.en: And one of the ideas that we played with here was the idea of being able to give gold to other players. It was like, wouldn't this kind of lead to all sorts of interesting possibilities if we put into the game the ability to give gold to other players? You could say, I'll give you this much gold if you do this for me, or I feel sorry for you. I'm going to give you 300 gold. Or, hey, please give me some gold, or whatever.
cues.zh: 我们在这里尝试的一个想法是，能让玩家把金币赠予其他玩家。设想一下，如果游戏中加入了赠送金币的功能，岂不是会引发各种有趣的可能性？你可以说，帮我做这件事，我就给你这么多金币；或者出于同情，我赠你300金币；又或者，嘿，能不能给我点金币，诸如此类。

cues.en: There would be this fascinating kind of diplomatic negotiating dynamic that would arise in the game. What we found, however, was that nobody ever gave gold to anybody else. The thought did not cross their mind to give gold to other people. I don't know what this says about the human condition or the future of mankind, but it's kind of a sad, sad commentary, I think.
cues.zh: 这样一来，游戏中就会出现一种迷人的外交谈判动态。然而，我们发现，根本没人给过别人金币。他们压根没想到要给其他人金币。我不清楚这反映了人性的哪个方面或人类的未来会怎样，但这在我看来，是个相当悲哀的注解。

cues.en: Another bad idea that I had. Okay, one of the things that I kind of promised in the blurb to this presentation was to explain how to save millions of dollars in game design. And so if you're interested in that part of the presentation, this would be the time to pay attention. One of the techniques I think that's very important in making AAA games on a shoestring
cues.zh: 我另一个不太好的主意。好吧，我在这次演讲简介中承诺的一件事，就是要讲解如何在游戏设计中节省数百万美元。所以，如果你对这部分内容感兴趣，现在就得留心了。我认为，在低成本制作AAA级游戏时，一个非常重要的技巧

cues.en: is to really use the player's imagination as a very key tool. No matter how good your graphics are, no matter how cool your technology is, what's happening in the player's mind, the player can always visualize something more compelling and more dynamic. So the goal of everything we do is to make something happen in the player's imagination that is really cool.
cues.zh: 就是真正把玩家的想象力作为一个关键工具来利用。无论你的画面有多好，技术有多酷，玩家脑海中发生的一切，总能构想出更加引人入胜、更为生动的东西。因此，我们所做的一切目的，就是要激发玩家想象中那些真正精彩绝伦的场景。

cues.en: and often we don't have to literally show everything in the game to make that happen. If the player can imagine what's going on, you know, imagine what Napoleon is doing when he's not actually on the screen, imagine what's going on behind the scenes, then we save a lot of money by not having to create all those assets and do all those things. And one example, again, from Civilization Revolution is this screen here. It says, foreign rulers
cues.zh: 很多时候我们不必真的把游戏里的一切都展示出来才能做到这一点。如果玩家能自己想象发生了什么，比如想象拿破仑不在屏幕上时在做什么，想象幕后发生的事，那我们就不用制作那些素材、做那些事，能省下很多钱。再举一个《文明革命》里的例子，就是这个界面。上面写着：外国统治者

cues.en: seek your favor, the Sultan of Zanzibar sends you a caravan of exotic gifts, including seven dancing bears. The principle here is something I call go with the flow. In other words, if it's something the player is already inclined to believe, if it's something the player wants to believe, it's very easy to make that happen in the player's imagination. The player looks at this and says, oh, yeah, foreign leaders should be seeking my favor.
cues.zh: 寻求你的青睐，桑给巴尔苏丹送来一队异国礼物，包括七只会跳舞的熊。这里的原理我叫它顺水推舟。换句话说，如果某件事玩家本来就倾向于相信，如果某件事玩家愿意相信，那就很容易在玩家的想象中实现。玩家看到这个会说，哦对，外国领袖就该来寻求我的青睐。

cues.en: it's out of gifts. Cool. They should be sending me again. And seven dancing bearers. That's very cool. So it's happening. In your mind, the bearers are dancing. It's all happening up there. Because I'm inclined to agree with this sentiment right here. And we actually don't have any dancing bearers. There's no Sultan of Zanzibar. There's no caravan. But by going with the flow, we've saved ourselves millions of dollars in not having to create all these
cues.zh: 还送礼物，酷。他们该再来送礼。还有七只会跳舞的熊，太酷了。于是这事就成了。在你脑海里，那些熊在跳舞，一切都在你脑子里上演。因为我本来就倾向于认同这里的说法。而我们其实根本没有会跳舞的熊。没有桑给巴尔苏丹，没有商队。但靠顺水推舟，我们省下了数百万美元，不用去制作所有这些

cues.en: models and textures and assets and all this kind of stuff because the player wants to believe this and all we have done is basically put up a text box. Now that allows us to save our resources, our time, our energy for the things that are kind of harder to sell, the things that the player might not be so inclined to believe or kind of want to see brought to life with all sorts of cool graphical stuff.
cues.zh: 模型、贴图、素材之类的东西，因为玩家愿意相信这些，而我们做的其实只是放了一个文本框。这样一来，我们就能把资源、时间和精力省下来，用在那些比较难让人买账的东西上，那些玩家可能不太愿意相信、或者不太愿意看到用各种炫酷图形效果呈现出来的东西上。

cues.en: Another technique for saving millions and millions of dollars in designing games is to use, take advantage of what the player already knows. Players bring lots of their own information to games and they don't have to, a lot of that doesn't have to be reinforced literally. Pirates, for example, a game where people bring a lot of their own knowledge to the game. So if they see a
cues.zh: 在设计游戏时节省数百万美元的另一个技巧，就是利用玩家已有的知识。玩家会自带大量信息进入游戏，很多内容不必逐字逐句地强化说明。比如海盗题材的游戏，玩家会带入很多自己的知识。所以当他们看到

cues.en: swordsman with a black curly mustache. They probably know that it's going to be the evil meta villain that they're going to have to sword fight and we don't need a whole lot of back story to explain how he got that way and what his childhood was like, et cetera, et cetera. Black curly mustache, okay, bad guy, time for a sword fight. Millions of dollars saved in back story. So these are just a couple of techniques by which
cues.zh: 一个留着黑色卷曲八字胡的剑客，大概就知道这是邪恶的大反派，接下来要跟他比剑，我们不需要大段背景故事来解释他怎么变成这样、童年经历如何等等。黑色卷曲八字胡，好，坏人，该比剑了。省下数百万美元的背景故事开销。这些只是几个技巧，

cues.en: You can kind of focus, I think, your energy and your resources on what's going to be really impressive, what's going to be new, and what's going to be hard to sell in the game, and take advantage of things that the players kind of going to almost automatically provide through their own imagination. Let's talk about artificial intelligence for a moment. AI is often a place where psychology really comes strongly into play.
cues.zh: 让你能把精力和资源集中在真正惊艳、真正新颖、以及游戏里难卖的部分，同时利用玩家几乎会自动通过想象力补全的东西。接下来聊聊人工智能。AI 往往是心理学强烈发挥作用的地方。

cues.en: because the AI kind of represents your opponent, the enemy. And whenever you're in a kind of conflict situation, your psychological juices are flowing even more strongly. You're really committed and invested in that conflict. And so a lot of players project a lot onto the AI because they feel it's this competitive situation. And there's a number of different philosophies about AI.
cues.zh: 因为 AI 代表着你的对手、敌人。每当你处于冲突情境中，心理反应会更加强烈。你会真正投入这场冲突。所以很多玩家会对 AI 投射大量情感，因为他们觉得这是竞争关系。关于 AI，有多种不同的理念。

cues.en: And my point of view is not necessarily the only point of view. There may be other points of view. But I look at AI as one element in creating an integrated overall experience for the player. In a single player game, like most of the games we're talking about, again, the star of the game, the key experience is the experience that the player is having.
cues.zh: 我的观点未必是唯一正确的。可能还有别的看法。但我把 AI 看作是为玩家打造一体化整体体验的一个要素。在单人游戏里，就像我们讨论的大多数游戏一样，游戏的主角、核心体验就是玩家所经历的那种体验。

cues.en: And so AI is kind of a tool to craft that experience, to customize it, to make it seem even more real to the player. There's another point of view which is that the AI should act like another player, another person, should have humanish characteristics and should feel like another player. I don't actually subscribe to that philosophy. There's a couple things that I've seen that make me shy away from that. I'm not saying it's absolutely the wrong idea.
cues.zh: 所以 AI 算是一种工具，用来雕琢这种体验、定制它，让玩家觉得更真实。还有另一种观点认为，AI 应该像另一个玩家、另一个人，具备类人特征，让人感觉是另一个玩家。我其实并不认同这种理念。我见过的一些情况让我对此敬而远之。我不是说这想法绝对错误。

cues.en: But in my experience, if an AI has human characteristics, one thing we talk about is I want it to surprise me. I want it to be tricky and clever. When AI does that, most players feel that it's being stupid. It's dumb because there's a fine line between clever and dumb.
cues.zh: 但依我的经验，如果 AI 具备人类特征——我们常提到的一点是我希望它能给我惊喜，我希望它狡猾又聪明。可当 AI 这么做时，大多数玩家会觉得它很蠢。它很傻，因为聪明和愚蠢之间只有一线之隔。

cues.en: and the player is inclined to see the AI as being dumb. If the AI does something really brilliant, the player will assume that the AI peeked behind the scenes and looked at my numbers and looked where my stuff was and cheated, basically. So there's a lot of kind of psychological stuff that goes on if the AI acts in ways that are kind of out of the norm. And they generally
cues.zh: 而且玩家倾向于认为 AI 很蠢。如果 AI 做了什么非常出彩的事，玩家就会认定 AI 在幕后偷看，看了我的数值、看了我的东西在哪，基本上就是在作弊。所以如果 AI 的行为方式有点不合常规，就会产生很多心理层面的东西。而这些通常

cues.en: lead to the player kind of jumping out, losing that suspension of disbelief and blaming the AI for what's going on in the game. So the way that I approach AI is to make it almost a metric, kind of a solid competition against which you play.
cues.zh: 会让玩家一下子出戏，失去那种悬置怀疑的状态，把游戏里发生的事归咎于 AI。所以我对待 AI 的方式，是把它几乎做成一个指标，一种你可以与之对抗的稳定竞争。

cues.en: but which you can kind of feel and your advancement as you go on. You get this real sense of progress. There's this improvement metric that the AI is kind of predictable, kind of solid and steady.
cues.zh: 但你能感觉到自己一路上的进步。你会真切地感到自己在成长。这个进步指标让 AI 显得有点可预测，但也稳定、扎实。

cues.en: And you're the one doing the brilliant things and the clever things and getting better and better versus the AI. Another thing that AI can do is give you feedback when you're talking to the leaders in civilization. They often comment upon what you're doing and how, you know, whether it's good or bad or whether they like it or don't like it. When we're playing a single player game, kind of feedback, validation is really important because you're kind of the only person there.
cues.zh: 而做出精彩、聪明之举、相对 AI 越来越强的，是你。AI 还能做的另一件事，是在你和文明领袖交谈时给你反馈。他们经常会评论你在做什么、做得怎么样，是好是坏，或者他们喜不喜欢。我们玩单人游戏时，这种反馈和认可非常重要，因为那儿差不多只有你一个人。

cues.en: And these AI characters are kind of your only friends at that point in time. So having them acknowledge what you're doing, be aware of it, is really validating for the player and is something we found in Civil Revolution was really important. The more that the other leaders in the game kind of reflected on what you were doing and reacted, the more the player felt that somebody understood them. You know what I'm going through. And they weren't just kind of playing in a vacuum. They were playing in a
cues.zh: 而在那个时点，这些 AI 角色差不多就是你唯一的朋友。所以，让它们认可你正在做的事、注意到这些，对玩家来说是极大的肯定；这也是我们在 Civil Revolution 里发现非常重要的一点。游戏里的其他领袖越是能对你在做的事有所反映并作出回应，玩家就越觉得有人理解自己，知道自己正在经历什么。而且他们不是在一个真空里游玩。他们是在一个

cues.en: interesting world. I talked a little bit earlier about self-destructive behavior. Ways that the player actually can damage their gameplay experience. And one of the responsibilities that I think we have as designers is to protect the player from themselves.
cues.zh: 有趣的世界里。我前面稍微谈过自我毁灭行为。也就是玩家实际上可能损害自己游戏体验的方式。而我认为，作为设计师，我们的责任之一，就是保护玩家不伤害自己。

cues.en: And there are a couple of ways or places where this really becomes an issue. One is how do you handle the idea of load and save. I've watched people play civilization where before every battle they save the game, if they don't win, they reload that save game, play the battle again, save it until they win the game. To me that's not really playing the game that I designed. That's not the experience
cues.zh: 有几个方面或场景确实会带来问题。其中之一是如何处理存档与读档。我见过有人玩《文明》，每场战斗前先存档，没赢就读档重打，再存档，直到打赢为止。对我来说，这根本不算在玩我设计的游戏。这不是我认为最有趣的体验。

cues.en: that I think is most interesting. It really doesn't require you to have a flexible strategy. It doesn't kind of require you to think ahead. If you know you're going to win every battle, the game I think is a lot less fun. So in Civilization Revolution, we actually save the random number with the save file. So if you reload the save file, you get the same result in your battle. Ha, ha, ha. That'll teach you. I guess people did find a way to get around that.
cues.zh: 它其实并不要求你采用灵活的策略，也不要求你提前思考。如果你知道自己每场战斗都会赢，游戏在我看来就乏味得多。所以在《文明革命》里，我们实际上把随机数一起存进了存档。这样你读档后，战斗结果还是一样的。哈哈哈，这下长记性了吧。不过我想玩家还是找到了绕过它的办法。

cues.en: By providing the player perhaps too easy access to loading and saving, you may actually be diminishing the experience for the player, and that is something to think about in game design. In Pirates, we actually only allow you to load and save the game when you're in a port. As you voyage around, you need to live with the consequences of that voyage. And kind of by building it into the fantasy of the game, I think it's a little less
cues.zh: 如果让玩家太容易读档存档，你反而可能削弱玩家的体验，这是游戏设计中值得思考的一点。在《海盗》里，我们只允许你在港口时存档读档。在海上航行时，你就得承担航行的后果。而且把这一点融入游戏的幻想设定中，我觉得就不那么

cues.en: obvious that we are trying to kind of control your load save behavior. But that's something to think about is finding ways to build your load save restrictions kind of into the fantasy, the story of the game. Another area where I think we can damage the gameplay experience for the player is in providing them too many options, settings, things that they can kind of customize in the middle of the game.
cues.zh: 明显地看出我们在试图控制你的存档读档行为了。所以值得思考的是，想办法把存档读档的限制融入游戏的幻想和故事里。另一个可能损害玩家游戏体验的方面，是给他们太多选项、设置，以及可以在游戏中途自定义的东西。

cues.en: There's all sorts of good things that the player should be able to customize. Whether you think the joystick works this way, whether you're left handed or right handed. All those things are key. But there's been a tendency that I think has kind of gone away more recently, but to kind of open up all sorts of game play decisions to the player. And to me, that's kind of wrong. As designers, we're here to make the game.
cues.zh: 玩家应该有各种可以自定义的东西。比如你觉得摇杆这样操作对不对，你是左撇子还是右撇子。这些都是关键。以前有一种倾向，就是把各种玩法决策都开放给玩家，不过最近我觉得这种倾向已经慢慢消失了。但在我看来，这其实是错的。作为设计师，我们是来做游戏的。

cues.en: and not to kind of hand it over to the player and say, I'm not sure how this game should work. You figure it out. So kind of being careful with the types of things that you open up to player is one thing to think about. Another is cheat codes. Again, I think it's a way that players can actually damage the gameplay experience for themselves. I remember when we were working on Civilization II,
cues.zh: 而不是把游戏甩给玩家说，我也不确定这游戏该怎么运作，你自己琢磨吧。所以要谨慎考虑把哪些东西开放给玩家，这是第一点。另一点是作弊码。我觉得作弊码其实会让玩家自己破坏自己的游戏体验。我记得我们做《文明2》的时候，

cues.en: I looked at, Brian Reynolds brought the game and I looked at it and there on the main menu was cheat. It was like play a quick game, play a random map, play a game, cheat. And I said, you know, Brian, cheat. You know, on the main menu, yeah, it's cool. You know, you can bring in tanks in the middle ages and run over people and, you know, it's cool. And I don't disagree that it's cool.
cues.zh: Brian Reynolds把游戏拿过来，我一看，主菜单上赫然写着“作弊”。就像这样：快速游戏、随机地图、开始游戏、作弊。我就说，Brian，作弊？在主菜单上？他说，对啊，很酷啊。你可以在中世纪弄出坦克来碾人，很酷。我也不否认这很酷。

cues.en: In fact, I watched my son when he was playing, you know, have a wonderful time bringing in all these tanks and running roughshod over the pikemen in the Middle Ages. But it's like, but Brian, you know, does the main menu, can't we just bury it one or two levels deeper? Because, you know, I kind of want the players to play the real game first before they start experimenting with the cheats and the Easter eggs and things like that.
cues.zh: 事实上，我看我儿子玩的时候，弄来一堆坦克，在中世纪的长枪兵身上横冲直撞，玩得可开心了。但我说，Brian，主菜单上……我们能不能至少把它藏深一两层？因为我希望玩家先好好玩真正的游戏，然后再去折腾作弊码、彩蛋之类的东西。

cues.en: The good news is that this cheating idea actually led directly to the idea of modding, which is very powerful. Certainly, with Civilization II, it was a breakthrough for Civilization and added incredible amount of variety and energy to the Civilization series. This is a picture from Fall from Heaven. And so, there's a happy ending to the story of cheats.
cues.zh: 好消息是，这种作弊思路其实直接催生了“模组改造”的概念，而它非常强大。当然，在《文明II》中，这对《文明》系列是一次突破，为整个系列增添了难以置信的多样性和活力。这是一张来自《Fall from Heaven》的图片。所以，作弊的故事有个圆满的结局。

cues.en: And modding has been a very cool addition, kind of allowing players to exercise their inner designer and become part of the community process. So cheating, I'm not so sure, but modding is definitely a cool thing. So another kind of psychological skill I think that we need to develop as designers is listening to the player.
cues.zh: 模组改造是个很酷的附加功能，让玩家能够发挥内心的设计师潜能，成为社区进程的一部分。所以作弊嘛，我不太确定，但模组改造绝对是个很酷的东西。作为设计师，我认为我们需要培养的另一种心理技能就是倾听玩家。

cues.en: I'm kind of assuming at this point that you've bought into the idea that game design is an iterative process, you know, starting with the prototype and kind of building on that, getting a lot of play, getting a lot of feedback, building a game over time. And if you do that, you're going to spend a lot of time talking to the players, the people that are playing your game, getting their feedback and taking advantage of that to make your game better.
cues.zh: 到这里，我假设你已经接受了游戏设计是一个迭代过程这个理念——从原型开始，在此基础上不断构建，进行大量试玩，获取大量反馈，随着时间推移把游戏做出来。如果你这么做，就会花很多时间和玩家交流，也就是那些在玩你游戏的人，获取他们的反馈并加以利用，让你的游戏变得更好。

cues.en: But what I found in that process is that it's really not that useful to kind of take literally what your players are saying to you. There are different kind of ways that players will react to the game. One is to kind of provide you with solutions. I think you should take this out. I think you should change this. I think this should work this way.
cues.zh: 但在这个过程中我发现，完全字面地理解玩家对你说的话其实并不太有用。玩家对游戏的反应有几种不同方式。一种是直接给你提供解决方案：我觉得你应该把这个去掉，我觉得你应该改改这个，我觉得这个应该这样运作。

cues.en: that's useful, but a lot of times that really doesn't take into account other parts of the game that that would break, et cetera, et cetera. And it's tempting to kind of discard that, you know, that's not going to work. I know that's not going to work. You might have even tried that. But I think it's important as a designer to get some real value out of that, to drill down to what is motivating that solution. What is wrong? What is the kind of
cues.zh: 这很有用，但很多时候它并没有考虑到游戏里其他会被弄坏的部分，等等等等。然后很容易就想把它丢掉，你知道，“这行不通。我知道这行不通。”你甚至可能已经试过了。但我觉得作为设计师，重要的是从中获取真正的价值，深入挖掘是什么在推动那个解决方案。问题出在哪？是什么让

cues.en: thing that the player is feeling or doing that is unsatisfying that leads them to kind of suggest the solution. And a lot of times you can find something that is consistent with your game design and your game ideas that will solve that problem for them. It might not be the exact solution that they proposed, but it will solve the problem and everybody is happy. Another type of comment that you might get back is kind of the opposite of that. It's an emotion. It doesn't feel right.
cues.zh: 玩家感到或做出不满足的体验，导致他们提出那个解决方案。很多时候你能找到与你的游戏设计和游戏理念一致的东西，来解决他们的问题。它可能不是他们提出的确切方案，但能解决问题，大家都满意。你可能收到的另一种反馈则恰恰相反。它是一种情绪。“感觉不对。”

cues.en: I'm frustrated, I'm confused. Again, very little information. And again, it's kind of our job as designers to figure out what is it that's causing that emotion. What can I change to make that emotion go away if it's a bad emotion or to strengthen that if it's a positive emotion. Another important, oops, don't look at that slide.
cues.zh: “我很沮丧，我很困惑。”同样，信息很少。同样，作为设计师，我们的工作就是弄清楚是什么导致了这种情绪。如果是不好的情绪，我能改变什么来消除它；如果是积极的情绪，又该怎么强化它。另一个重要的，哎呀，别看那张幻灯片。

cues.en: The last thing I think is important about talking to your players is knowing their individual personalities. A lot of times it's very helpful in deciphering, decoding what they're saying because a certain player might not like that type of game and is never going to be happy. There are certain players we call Mr. Anecdotal who will be convinced something has happened that you know is impossible but will just kind of harp on that one thing that
cues.zh: 关于和玩家交流，我觉得最后重要的一点是了解他们各自的性格。很多时候这对解读、破译他们说的话非常有帮助，因为某个玩家可能不喜欢这类游戏，永远不会满意。有些玩家我们叫他们“轶事先生”，他们会坚信发生了某件事，而你知道那是不可能的，但就是会揪着那一件事不放，

cues.en: that there are people that are very generous, you know, kind of afraid to say anything bad about the game. You almost have to force them. I know you hated something about it. Come, tell me, tell me what it is. So kind of knowing the personalities of your players is important in, again, in deciphering what they're really trying to tell you. And kind of really tapping into this resource, which is really invaluable, the gameplay experience of your testers as you're playing the game.
cues.zh: 有些人非常宽容，你知道，有点不敢说游戏的坏话。你几乎得逼他们。“我知道你有不喜欢的地方。来，告诉我，告诉我是什么。”所以，了解玩家的性格对于解读他们真正想告诉你的东西很重要。要真正利用好这个资源，它真的非常宝贵，那就是测试者在玩游戏时的游玩体验。

cues.en: So what is the point of all this, you might be asking? Kind of like to wrap it up with this idea of the epic journey. I think this is what we're trying to create for the player, is an epic journey. I think I should trademark this one, too. Epic journey. Keep that in. There's so many genres, so many styles of games, so many different ways of gaming.
cues.zh: 你可能会问，这一切的意义是什么？我想用“史诗之旅”这个概念来收尾。我觉得这就是我们想为玩家创造的东西——一段史诗之旅。这个我也该注册商标。“史诗之旅”。保留这句。游戏有那么多类型、那么多风格、那么多不同的玩法。

cues.en: But I think in a way they can kind of all be encapsulated in this idea of an epic journey. And how do we use psychology to make our journey more epic and our epic more journey-like? You might be asking. Here are a couple of tools that we have to make that happen. I come back again and again to the idea of interesting decisions. That's really
cues.zh: 但我觉得在某种程度上，它们都可以被囊括进“史诗之旅”这个概念里。那我们如何用心理学让我们的旅程更史诗、让我们的史诗更像旅程呢？你可能会问。这里有几个工具能帮我们做到。我一次又一次回到“有趣的决定”这个想法上。那才是

cues.en: the core, the basic fundamental pieces of your game are these decisions that you're giving the player. And the process, the journey is the process of exploring all these decisions and seeing how they relate to each other and playing through them. So think about the decisions that you're giving your player. Are they ones that encourage them to project, to think into the future? If I do this, what is going to happen?
cues.zh: 核心，是你游戏最基本的基础构件——你给玩家的这些决定。而这个过程、这段旅程，就是探索所有这些决定、看它们如何相互关联、并逐一体验的过程。所以想想你给玩家的决定。它们是否鼓励玩家去投射、去思考未来？如果我这么做，会发生什么？

cues.en: Do they have interesting, kind of not taken paths? The coolest decisions are the ones where the player chooses path A, but they're kind of saying, well, next time, you know, that path B looks kind of interesting, too, so I'm going to play next time and try that other path. Those are the really powerful decisions. If you can build them into your game, you're well on your way to creating the epic journey. Learning and progress.
cues.zh: 它们是否有有趣的、未被选择的路径？最酷的决定，是玩家选了路径A，但心里想着：嗯，下次那条路径B看起来也挺有意思的，所以我下次要玩一遍试试另一条路。那些才是真正强大的决定。如果你能把它们构建进游戏里，你就已经走在创造史诗之旅的路上了。学习与成长。

cues.en: This is fundamental to the journey. The idea that you are constantly progressing. You're constantly at a better place than you were before. You're smarter than you were before. You're more powerful. It's kind of fundamental, but it's easy to lose track of this. I think you cannot reward and acknowledge and reflect this progress too much in a game. It's very important for the player to know
cues.zh: 这是这段旅程的根本。就是你在不断进步的想法。你一直处在比以前更好的位置。你比以前更聪明。你更强大。这很根本，但很容易忽略。我觉得在游戏里，对进步的奖励、认可和反馈再多也不为过。让玩家知道

cues.en: how they're doing, what value has this last half hour been to me in terms of playing. I think World of Warcraft does a great job of this. The level system makes it very clear the kind of progress you made and their ways of building this idea, which is very powerful into your game. One more turn. This is another way of making the journey epic.
cues.zh: 自己做得怎么样，过去半小时的游戏对我有什么价值，这非常重要。《魔兽世界》在这方面做得很好。等级系统让你清楚看到自己取得了怎样的进展，他们把这套理念有力融入游戏的方式也很值得借鉴。“再来一回合”，这是让旅程变得史诗感的另一种方式。

cues.en: It's a concept that we relate back to civilization, but it applies to almost every game. The idea that the player is constantly kind of leaning forward. They're anticipating things that are going to happen later. They're looking forward to their plans coming together. They're wondering what's around the next corner. You can foreshadow. You can kind of just let people know that cool stuff is going to happen soon. And it draws them very much into this one more turn phenomenon.
cues.zh: 这个概念我们会联系到《文明》，但它几乎适用于所有游戏。就是玩家始终在向前探身。他们在期待之后会发生的事。他们盼着自己的计划逐步实现。他们好奇下一个转角有什么。你可以做铺垫。你可以直接让人知道好东西马上就要来了。这会把他们深深拉进“再来一回合”的现象里。

cues.en: And it kind of all comes back to this idea of replayability, that if you create a fantastic journey and the player comes to enter that journey, they suddenly realize that this is only one segment of this epic journey. This journey is much more epic than they even thought because this has only been a part. The epic was a part. It's like epic squared or epic cubed. This journey is multi-epic.
cues.zh: 这一切又回到可重玩性的理念：如果你创造了一段精彩的旅程，玩家进入之后会突然意识到，这只是这段史诗旅程的一个片段。这段旅程比他们想象的还要史诗得多，因为此前经历的只是一部分。史诗也只是其中一部分。就像史诗的平方，甚至史诗的立方。这段旅程是多重史诗。

cues.en: And replayability kind of plants that seed and makes that happen for your game. So these are some tools, some psychological tools that make your game the coolest epic journey of all time. So now you know everything. Thank you. We have a little bit of time for questions. There are some folks with microphones. I'm sure.
cues.zh: 可重玩性会埋下这颗种子，让你的游戏实现这一点。这些心理工具能让你的游戏成为史上最酷、最史诗般的旅程。现在你们什么都知道了，谢谢大家。我们还有一点时间回答问题。现场有几位拿着麦克风的工作人员，我相信……

cues.en: much of what I've said has been wrong and you're going to correct me on it. But I'd be happy to take any questions or thoughts. If there's anybody who would like to ask a question. Look for someone with a green, raise your hand and look for somebody with a green shirt and a microphone. Right here. What do you normally tell your animators, designers, artists, exactly how you want
cues.zh: 我刚才说的很多内容可能都是错的，你们肯定会来纠正我。不过我很乐意回答大家的问题，或者听听你们的想法。有人想提问吗？找一位穿绿色衣服、拿着麦克风的人。就在这边。你通常会怎么告诉动画师、设计师和美术人员，你希望某款游戏的美术呈现出什么感觉？你会怎样向他们说明你的构想？

cues.en: the art for particular games to feel? How do you explain to them what you have in your vision? The question is how do I explain to animators and artists what my vision is, what I want them to do? There's a couple dimensions to that. A lot of times I will actually build a prototype myself using pieces from other games and things like that that kind of create the big picture so they know what
cues.zh: 问题是，我怎样向动画师和美术人员说明我的构想，以及我希望他们做什么？这要从几个方面来说。很多时候，我会用其他游戏里的素材之类的东西，亲自搭一个原型，先把整体构想呈现出来，让他们知道自己做的东西如何融入整体。

cues.en: how what they're doing fits into the bigger picture. One of the issues, I think, with art is often it's easy to get kind of key hold and only focus on the one thing that you're making. The other thing that I think is important is to kind of let your artist be artists, be creative. Put a pretty big box around what you want and let them surprise you with something that's even cooler than you imagined.
cues.zh: 我觉得美术工作有个问题：人很容易只盯着手头正在做的那一件事，只关注局部。另一件重要的事，是让美术人员做自己，发挥创造力。把你的要求划定一个大致范围，然后给他们空间，让他们用比你想象中更酷的创意带给你惊喜。

cues.en: So one is having a prototype that they can always go back to if the question is, how does this fit into the game? What is it supposed to do? But then let them be artists. I think that games as a collaborative medium really need to take advantage of all the talents that you have available to work on it. So I try to let the artists be as creative as they can be. Question?
cues.zh: 所以，我们会准备一个原型，方便大家随时回头确认：这东西放进游戏里合不合适？它应该做什么？但之后就让美术人员自由发挥。我觉得，游戏作为一种协作媒介，真的应该充分发挥参与制作的每个人的才能。所以我尽量让美术人员发挥创造力。有什么问题吗？

cues.en: you talked about player egoism and that sort of approach to that players come come to approach games with and I guess I'm having a hard time like figuring out like do you think that you know this egoistic approach to games is kind of prefigured by the themes that that you give them like
cues.zh: 你刚才谈到了玩家的自我中心，以及玩家玩游戏时抱着的这类心态。我有点想不明白：你觉得这种以自我为中心的游戏心态，是不是由你给游戏设定的主题预先塑造的？比如说……

cues.en: you're going to build a civilization, you're going to become a railroad tycoon, or do you sort of pick these themes because you anticipate that this is what players, like how players want to feel when they play a game? I think one of the fundamental attractions of gaming is that you can go to places that you can't go in real life, that you can inhabit characters that you probably don't have the opportunity to do in real life. And I think it's kind of the Walter Minnie fantasy. I get to be
cues.zh: 玩家要去建立一个文明，或者成为铁路大亨；还是说，你选这些主题，是因为你预料到玩家想在游戏里获得这样的感受？我觉得，游戏最根本的吸引力之一，就是你能去到现实生活中无法前往的地方，也能扮演现实中大概没机会成为的角色。我觉得这有点像沃尔特·米蒂式的幻想：我可以成为……

cues.en: a dashing swashbuckling pirate, you know, I get to run a great civilization. So we definitely look for topics that are epic, that are big, that kind of really empower the player and make them much larger than life because I think that's what you're looking for in a gameplay experience is something to kind of take you out of the real world and into a cooler world. Take you out of your real life into a cooler life, take you out of maybe your real character into a cooler character.
cues.zh: 一个潇洒勇猛的海盗，或者经营一个伟大的文明。所以我们确实会寻找宏大、史诗般的题材，让玩家感到更有力量，仿佛超越了凡人。因为我觉得，玩家想要的游戏体验，就是暂时离开现实世界，进入一个更酷的世界；离开现实生活，体验更酷的人生；也许还能摆脱现实中的自己，成为一个更酷的角色。

cues.en: Epic is definitely part of our thinking in putting together these game worlds because they are, I think at the end of the day, you know, that journey just feels cooler if it's been through thousands of years of history or through the heart of the Spanish main and ending up with that horribly evil guy with a mustache, you know, et cetera. So, yes, we definitely choose kind of epic larger than life situations.
cues.zh: Epic 绝对是我们在构建这些游戏世界时的考量之一，因为我觉得归根结底，如果这段旅程穿越了数千年的历史，或者穿过西班牙大陆的核心地带，最后遇到那个留着小胡子的邪恶家伙，你知道的等等，那种感觉就是更酷。所以，是的，我们确实会选择那种史诗般、超越现实的场景。

cues.en: because I think it makes a more compelling game. And it also taps into a lot of common knowledge and fantasy, which we can then use in building the game. Question over here. Hey, with a limited amount of time that people have to play games like as an adult, wouldn't it make more sense to make a single epic journey rather than having them play through it like two to the end times? I think people appreciate
cues.zh: 因为我觉得这能让游戏更有吸引力。而且它还能利用大量常识和幻想元素，我们可以在构建游戏时加以利用。这边有个问题。嘿，考虑到成年人玩游戏的时间有限，做一个单一的史诗旅程，而不是让他们玩两遍通关，是不是更合理？我觉得人们还是看重

cues.en: the value of replayability. I mean, there are sequels out there. So if you had a great experience with a game, you often want to do it again. I don't think people do have a limited amount of time to play games, but I think they select what games they want to play in that limited amount of time. And it's even more important for that reason that they're playing a game that they like. So replayability kind of allows you to play a game that you know you're going to like with that limited amount of time that you have.
cues.zh: 重玩价值。我的意思是，市面上有续作。所以如果你在某款游戏中有过很棒的体验，你往往想再来一次。我不认为人们玩游戏的时间真的有限，但我觉得他们会在这有限的时间里挑选想玩的游戏。正因如此，他们玩的是自己喜欢的游戏，这就更为重要。所以重玩价值让你能在有限的时间里玩一款你知道自己会喜欢的游戏。

cues.en: Hello, I have a question about the flight simulator point you made earlier. I've worked on racing games for a while, and the last one we released was Midnight Club 4 last year, which critically got slammed because everybody thought it was too hard. And we worked really hard to make it so you didn't have to win to progress and succeed in the game, but the conception was that people were really, really frustrated when they weren't coming in first all the time.
cues.zh: 你好，我有一个关于你之前提到的飞行模拟器观点的问题。我做过一段时间赛车游戏，我们去年发布的最后一款是《午夜俱乐部4》，结果被批评得很惨，因为大家都觉得太难了。我们费了很大劲，让玩家不必非得赢也能在游戏里推进和成功，但玩家的感受是，当他们不能一直拿第一时，真的非常非常沮丧。

cues.en: And I was wondering if you had any advice or solutions for trying to condition the player to accept that they're not going to win all the time. You're definitely walking uphill there, walking into the wind. I think the expectation is out there that you're going to win. I think you have to do a lot of work to make it fun not to win. Certainly realism and authenticity are cool things, but you have to work hard to, I think,
cues.zh: 我想知道你是否有任何建议或解决方案，试图让玩家接受他们不会一直赢。这肯定是逆水行舟、迎风而上。我认为玩家普遍抱有会赢的预期。你得下很大功夫，才能让不赢也变得有趣。当然，真实感和原汁原味是好事，但我认为你得努力去

cues.en: to sell that idea. I'm a big Gran Turismo fan, but even that game, I think you still end up winning very often, even though it has the real feel of authenticity. Good luck, but that's a tough one. Over here. Hi. You were talking about how it's really good to
cues.zh: 推销这个理念。我是《GT赛车》的忠实粉丝，但即便是那款游戏，我觉得你最终还是会经常赢，尽管它确实有真实的质感。祝你好运，但这确实很难。这边。你好。你刚才谈到用选择来

cues.en: prison the player with choices. And when it comes to a lot of games lately, they've been doing a lot of the moral choices like good or evil. Is it more positive to do that and have the player expect a certain outcome or would you rather see games start moving into the morally gray area where it's more uncertain? That's a good question. I am not a fan of morally gray games. I think that this alliance, this unholy alliance that we made with the player to me excludes that unless you're very clear up front.
cues.zh: 困住玩家，这非常好。而最近很多游戏都在做大量的道德选择，比如善或恶。这样做并让玩家预期某个特定结果，是不是更积极？还是你更希望看到游戏开始进入道德灰色的地带，更加不确定？这是个好问题。我不是道德灰色游戏的粉丝。我认为我们与玩家建立的这种联盟，这种不神圣的联盟，在我看来排除了那种可能，除非你一开始就说得非常清楚。

cues.en: that this is a game about gray moral choices, because you're asking the player to invest this time. One of the analogies I use is like showing up on your first day at high school. You're kind of wondering, what are the rules here? Who are the cool people? How does this place work? And so you're kind of very vulnerable early in the game, and you want to kind of be encouraged and kind of know that this time that you're investing and spending is taking you down the right path.
cues.zh: 这是个关于灰色道德选择的游戏，因为你在要求玩家投入时间。我常用的一个类比是高中开学第一天。你会想，这里的规矩是什么？谁是比较酷的人？这地方怎么运作？所以游戏初期你会很脆弱，你希望得到鼓励，想知道自己投入的时间正带你走上正确的路。

cues.en: And the idea of the morally gray choices and things like that, I think it always plants the idea in the player's mind that I might be on the wrong track here. All this time I'm investing now, this might be just taking me off in the wrong direction. And I think that's an opportunity for the player to kind of say, maybe I should try something else. I think you have to be very clear if your game is about morally gray, ambiguous choices that
cues.zh: 而道德灰色选择这类设定，我认为总会在玩家心里埋下“我可能走错路了”的念头。我现在投入的所有时间，也许正把我带偏。我觉得这正是玩家可以说“也许我该试试别的”的机会。如果你的游戏讲的是灰色、模糊的道德选择，那你就必须非常清楚，

cues.en: that you're going to make sure that wherever they go, something interesting is going to happen. That they're not going to be allowed to go off on some dead end path because they made a poor moral choice. Given the number of trends that you have seen come and go during the course of your career, what would you guess would be the next big trend in gaming? Where do you see the avant-garde idea coming from in the future?
cues.zh: 你要确保无论他们怎么走，都会发生有趣的事。不能因为他们做了糟糕的道德选择，就让他们走进死胡同。鉴于你职业生涯中见证过那么多趋势起起落落，你猜游戏界的下一个大趋势会是什么？你觉得未来的先锋理念会从哪儿来？

cues.en: It's a really cool time, I think, to be a game designer. We certainly have seen the indie games movement put a lot of new energy into gaming. We have new platforms, whether it's Facebook or the live places, browser games, a lot of places where the whole kind of big budget thing has gone away and opened up a lot of new opportunities for gaming.
cues.zh: 我觉得现在对游戏设计师来说是个很棒的时代。我们确实看到独立游戏运动给游戏业注入了大量新活力。我们有了新平台，无论是Facebook还是直播平台、浏览器游戏，很多地方那种大预算模式已经消失，为游戏开辟了许多新机会。

cues.en: Where do I see gaming going? I think this is the year of civilization, frankly. I think there's a civilization five maybe coming this year and a civilization network. So in the immediate future, I think this is the year of civilization. But looking further out, there's so much energy and dynamism, I think, in this industry.
cues.zh: 我看游戏业的走向如何？坦白说，我觉得今年是《文明》之年。今年可能会有《文明5》和《文明网络版》。所以短期内，我认为今年是《文明》之年。但往更远处看，这个行业里有太多活力和动力。

cues.en: that it's part of, I think, what keeps us, you know, every day looking to see what's new, and that's part of the big part of the excitement, I think, of being part of this industry. Over here. Hi. Throughout your presentation, you've talked a lot about how people hate failure in video games and avoid it. I would like you to speak a little bit more on how you can make a video game that just keeps getting better and better, or if that is possible,
cues.zh: 我认为这正是让我们每天都能看到新东西的部分原因，这也是身处这个行业令人兴奋的重要部分。这边。你好。在你的演讲中，你多次谈到人们在电子游戏里讨厌失败并会回避它。我想请你再谈谈如何做出一款不断变得更好的游戏，或者这是否可能，

cues.en: and how you personally avoid the feeling of losing or failure in the video game. I think almost every video game is built on the idea of progress. Now that doesn't mean that progress is free or automatic or guaranteed, but the player wants the basic experience to be one of getting better learning progressing. But the more that feels earned, the more satisfying it is.
cues.zh: 以及你个人如何避免在电子游戏里感受到失败或挫败。我认为几乎每款电子游戏都建立在“进步”这个理念上。这不意味着进步是免费的、自动的或有保证的，但玩家希望基本体验是不断变好、学习和进步。而越是感觉靠自己挣来的，就越有满足感。

cues.en: So in order for that to feel earned, there has to be the potential of a negative outcome, the potential of something bad happening. And when that happens, I think one of the key points is that the player understands why it happened and what the player can do to prevent that from happening the next time. I think that that's a win-win in many ways because the player is now thinking about another way of playing, about playing again, which you've also added to the value of the next piece of progress because it was one
cues.zh: 所以要让这种成就感名副其实，就必须存在负面结果的潜在可能，存在坏事发生的可能。而当这种情况发生时，我认为关键点之一是玩家要明白为什么会发生，以及下次怎样才能避免。我觉得这在很多方面都是双赢的，因为玩家现在会去思考另一种玩法、思考再玩一次，这也提升了你下一段进度的价值，因为它是在

cues.en: in spite of this adversity. So managing the kind of reward and punishment process is really fundamental to game design. Over here. Over here. Hello. Hi. You talked earlier about trying to maintain the player's idea of winning, always wanting to win, and the whole problem is arising with the load save issues. A lot of times when I was playing Civ, even though I'd win the game, it much became a point about trying to beat my own score.
cues.zh: 逆境中取得的。所以管理好这种奖励与惩罚的过程，对游戏设计来说真的很根本。这边，这边。你好。嗨。你之前谈到要维持玩家的获胜心态，总是想赢，而整个问题都出在读档存档上。我玩《文明》的时候很多次，即使我赢了游戏，它也更多变成了一个想打破自己分数的问题。

cues.en: And in order to do that, I had to take much more of an edge by, you know, and it did come down to that whole load save issues. I hated it when I lost a one, or there was something else I needed to get me to the next point. So my question to you is how do you accommodate your design when the player is not just trying to beat the machine, but beat themselves? I think that's another dimension of progress in one way, that you feel that progress against your own score. You know, whether you use the load save mechanism to do that or not, it's kind of your own
cues.zh: 为了做到这一点，我得冒更大的风险，你知道，而这确实就归结到了读档存档的问题上。我讨厌输掉一局，或者还差一点才能进入下一阶段。所以我的问题是，当玩家不只是想打败机器，而是想打败自己时，你如何在设计中兼顾这一点？我觉得从某种意义上说，这是进度的另一个维度，你会感到是在对抗自己的分数取得进步。你知道，你是否用读档存档机制来做到这一点，某种程度上是你自己的

cues.en: moral choice, I think. I mean, games give you many, many ways to play, and you get to pick the one that's hopefully most satisfying to you. Some of the talk about self-destructive behavior was kind of oriented towards, you know, maybe there's some things we shouldn't make that easy because at the end of the day, you might not feel as good about your victory if you use some of these things.
cues.zh: 道德选择，我觉得。我的意思是，游戏给了你很多很多玩法，你可以挑一个希望对自己来说最满意的。关于自我毁灭行为的一些讨论，某种程度上是在说，也许有些事情我们不该让它那么容易做到，因为归根结底，如果你用了这些东西，你可能对自己的胜利不会感觉那么好。

cues.en: We actually had these Iron Man modes. We would actually keep track of the number of load saves that you did. And that would be mentioned along with your score. So you could kind of, by doing it without loading and saving, for example, that would actually be something that would be noted on there and let you feel even better about your final score. Hi, Sid. Over here all the way to your left. In regards to the social network gaming,
cues.zh: 我们其实有这些钢铁侠模式。我们会记录你进行读档存档的次数。这个数据会和你的得分一起显示出来。所以你可以通过不读档存档来做到这一点，比如，这实际上会体现在那里，让你对最终得分感觉更好。嗨，Sid。就在这儿，一直往你的左边。关于社交网络游戏，

cues.en: There's a rampant kind of issue with cloning of games, so there's like 12 farm games and 22 island games and 73 sim games now. How do you foresee the protection of your IP or your kind of your big civilization network? Because it's an issue for everyone who's developing on social networks. That's definitely an issue.
cues.zh: 游戏克隆问题非常猖獗，所以现在有大约12款农场游戏、22款岛屿游戏和73款模拟游戏。你如何预见对你IP的保护，或者你的大型文明网络？因为这对每个在社交网络上开发的人来说都是个问题。这绝对是个问题。

cues.en: I think my role is to make the best game that I can make. We're playing the game almost daily right now, and we're putting in all sorts of cool stuff. So I think the way that we try and deal with that is to make the best game that we can. And in that way, make it very difficult to duplicate, because someone would have to go through that same testing experience and trying all the same dead ends that we tried that didn't work.
cues.zh: 我认为我的角色是做出我能做的最好的游戏。我们现在几乎每天都在玩这个游戏，我们正在加入各种酷炫的东西。所以我认为我们试图应对这个问题的方式就是做出我们能做的最好的游戏。这样一来，让它变得非常难以复制，因为别人必须经历同样的测试体验，尝试我们试过的所有同样行不通的死胡同。

cues.en: before getting to kind of the what does work. I think that question is, my role as a designer is just to make the best game I can make. What the industry does is kind of out of my hands, but I love my job, so I'm not complaining. Right here. Hi. Thanks for the talk. Loved it.
cues.zh: 才能找到真正可行的方案。我认为那个问题是，我作为设计师的角色就是做出我能做的最好的游戏。行业怎么做，我有点无法掌控，但我热爱我的工作，所以我不抱怨。就在这儿。嗨。感谢演讲。很喜欢。

cues.en: My question is about player expectations. Do you always have to acquiesce to these? Have you ever purposefully flown in the face of what the player expects?
cues.zh: 我的问题是关于玩家期望的。你总是必须迎合这些期望吗？你有没有故意违背玩家的期望？

cues.en: You're about the example of the math and the soldiers three versus one. Is there a deeper immersion achieved if a player's belief is rectified and he gains a feeling that he understands the player or the mechanic rather than just having a vague notion of math that he was using before? I think the fundamental purpose for dealing with the combat situation the way we did
cues.zh: 你刚才举了数学和士兵三对一的例子。如果玩家的信念被纠正，他获得一种感觉，觉得自己理解了玩家或机制，而不是仅仅对之前使用的数学有个模糊的概念，这样能实现更深的沉浸感吗？我认为我们处理战斗情境的根本目的

cues.en: was to not give the player a reason to jump out of the game to suspend their disbelief. That was kind of our primary goal. What I kind of realized, though, in going through that process, was that in some ways the player is actually right about what they're feeling.
cues.zh: 是不给玩家一个理由跳出游戏、中断他们的怀疑。这算是我们的首要目标。不过，在这个过程中我意识到，某种程度上玩家对他们感受的判断其实是对的。

cues.en: In a computer game, we say the odds are three to one, but the player isn't actually rolling the dice. They don't actually see that process. That's all happening somehow in some mysterious background code that some designer wrote that they may or may not trust. And so they're kind of at the mercy of the designer. So if bad things happen there that they can't see the reason for, this paranoia is really going to kick in.
cues.zh: 在电脑游戏中，我们说概率是三比一，但玩家实际上并没有在掷骰子。他们并没有真正看到这个过程。这一切都发生在某种神秘的背景代码中，那是某个设计师写的，他们可能信也可能不信。所以他们有点受制于设计师。所以如果那里发生了坏事，他们看不到原因，这种偏执就会真的发作。

cues.en: so that by making the odds that the outcomes kind of conform to what the players' expectations were, we kind of damp down this paranoia and also keep them in the game. So that was kind of the thinking process that we went through. We don't always try and meet the players' expectations exactly. I mean, there have to be surprises, have to be new things. You know, I put ballroom dancing into the new Pirates game. That was
cues.zh: 所以通过让概率使结果符合玩家的期望，我们某种程度上压制了这种偏执，也让他们留在游戏中。这就是我们经历的思考过程。我们并不总是试图完全满足玩家的期望。我的意思是，必须有惊喜，必须有新东西。你知道，我把交际舞放进了新的《海盗》游戏里。那是

cues.en: surprised a lot of people. Might have been one of the things on the my bad list. So we do try and surprise players. But not in kind of fundamental things that determine their success or failure. Thank you. Great talk. Kind of a follow-up to that question. In the way that your nine difficulty levels work, does the math get more honest at the higher difficulty levels? And second follow-up question, your personal preferences in gaming.
cues.zh: 让很多人惊讶的。可能是我失误清单上的事情之一。所以我们确实试图给玩家惊喜。但不是在决定他们成败的根本性事情上。谢谢。很棒的演讲。接着那个问题问一下。在你的九个难度级别的工作方式中，数学在更高难度级别会变得更诚实吗？第二个追问，你在游戏中的个人偏好。

cues.en: Do you enjoy games that are unabashedly difficult, like Demon's Souls? First question was, how are the difficulty levels implemented? There's no simple answer to that question. I think that, again, AI difficulty to me is a full range of tools that we use to create a customized experience for the player. The first difficulty level,
cues.zh: 你喜欢像 Demon's Souls 那样毫不掩饰地难的游戏吗？第一个问题是，难度等级是怎么实现的？这个问题没有简单答案。我还是觉得，对我来说，AI 难度是一整套工具，我们用它来为玩家创造定制化体验。第一个难度等级，

cues.en: is one that basically takes you on a tour through the game. You're probably going to win at the end, but you're going to get to see all the cool stuff that happens. And you'll understand that the next time it'll be more difficult. And with Civ in particular, the highest difficulty level is something that has to totally kick your butt every time or else you don't feel satisfied. It's a point of honor just to survive the highest level.
cues.zh: 基本上就是带你游览一遍游戏。你很可能会在最后获胜，但你能看到所有发生的酷东西。然后你会明白，下一次会更难。尤其是 Civ，最高难度每次都非得把你彻底打趴下，否则你就不觉得满足。能挺过最高难度本身就是一种荣誉。

cues.en: We're customizing those difficulty experiences using all sorts of different tools. Do I enjoy games that are very difficult? Generally not, I guess. The problem for me is I pick up a game and if I'm not really having fun in the first 15 or 20 minutes,
cues.zh: 我们用各种不同的工具来定制这些难度体验。我喜欢非常难的游戏吗？一般来说，我想并不喜欢。对我来说问题在于，我拿起一个游戏，如果前 15 或 20 分钟没有真正玩得开心，
