cues.en: I'm going to say I'm not going to really invest the 10 or 20 hours it's probably going to take to start to get some fun out of this game or really explore it. So I guess a pretty typical consumer in that fashion. Over here.
cues.zh: 我就会说，我不会真的投入大概要 10 或 20 小时，才开始从这个游戏里获得一些乐趣，或者真正探索它。所以我想，在这方面我算是挺典型的消费者。这边。

cues.en: During your slide presentation on MyBad and the design mistakes, there was a brief mention of an espionage game mechanic that you didn't feel was very interesting to talk about. Can you briefly summarize what that was and what you learned? We call that the covert action rule. Covert action was a game I wrote many, many years ago. And basically, it was an espionage game, and there was this kind of interestingly complex mystery that you were trying to unravel with
cues.zh: 在你关于 MyBad 和设计错误的幻灯片演示中，简短提到过一个间谍游戏机制，你觉得谈它不太有意思。你能简要概括那是什么，以及你学到了什么吗？我们称之为隐蔽行动规则。Covert Action 是我很多很多年前写的一个游戏。基本上，那是一个间谍游戏，里面有一种相当有趣的复杂谜团，你试图解开它，同时

cues.en: people in different cities doing different things to do dastardly things to the world and in the process of unraveling that mystery you would go into these action sequences where you would sneak through a building and open safes and clues and guards would chase you and you would follow cars around and you would unbreak codes and unravel these circuits, all sorts of cool action sequences and puzzles and based on our pirates experience we thought that was very cool. Pirates for us was a really neat
cues.zh: 不同城市里的人在做不同的事，对世界做卑鄙勾当；在解开这个谜团的过程中，你会进入这些动作段落：潜入一栋建筑，打开保险箱、寻找线索，警卫追你，你跟踪车辆，你破解密码、解开电路，各种很酷的动作段落和谜题。基于我们做 Pirates 的经验，我们觉得那非常酷。Pirates 对我们来说是一个非常巧妙的

cues.en: a combination of action and role-playing and strategy and all this kind of stuff working together. But what we found was that there were really two games fighting very hard against each other.
cues.zh: 动作、角色扮演和策略等元素的结合体，所有这些都在协同发挥作用。但我们发现，实际上有两个游戏在非常激烈地彼此对抗。

cues.en: that you were in the mystery part of the game and you were trying to put together the clues and figure things out and you say, okay, I need to go to Cairo and break into this building and that's going to take me to the next step of this mystery. And you do that and you kind of have this cool action sequence and you'd pop out of the building at the end, maybe five or ten minutes later and it's like, what was that mystery again? Why did I go into that building? And kind of the two games are not necessarily better than one was the
cues.zh: 你当时在游戏的悬疑部分，试图把线索拼凑起来弄清楚事情，然后你说，好吧，我得去开罗，闯进这栋楼，那会带我进入这个谜团的下一步。你照做了，经历了一段很酷的动作场面，最后从楼里出来，也许是五到十分钟之后，你就像，那个谜团是什么来着？我为什么进了那栋楼？这两部分游戏未必比只有一部分更好，这就是

cues.en: the rule, we call the covert action rule, is that the center of gravity of your game kind of has to be in one place. Everything else kind of supports that, enhances that, but you've got to figure out is the center of gravity in the action, is it in the strategy, you know, where, how does that all work? And when we look back at Pirates, we realize that the center of gravity of that game is kind of in the strategy, that the chip battles, the sword fights, et cetera, are kind of quick.
cues.zh: 那个规则，我们称之为隐蔽行动规则，就是你游戏的重心必须放在一个地方。其他一切都在支持它、增强它，但你得弄清楚重心是在动作上，还是在策略上，你知道，在哪里，这一切怎么运作？当我们回顾《海盗》时，我们意识到那个游戏的重心在策略上，芯片战斗、剑斗等等都很快。

cues.en: and clear enough that you don't lose the threat of what's going on when you come back to the strategy game. I think we have time for one more question. Is there someone? Yes. Thank you. When I was much younger, I had a lot of time to devote to playing your games. I loved the detail. And as I'm getting older and I'm getting all these responsibilities, I'm finding the detail overwhelming. So I'm wondering, is
cues.zh: 而且足够清晰，当你回到策略游戏时，你不会失去对当前局势的紧迫感。我想我们还有时间再问一个问题。有人吗？是的。谢谢。我年轻得多的时候，有很多时间投入玩你们的游戏。我喜欢那些细节。随着我变老，承担起各种责任，我发现细节让人不堪重负。所以我想知道，

cues.en: situation like mine, the aging gamer, is that playing a role in your game development process and how are you, if so, how are you dealing with it? I have to say yes. I mean, I'm an aging gamer myself and I think there are, we have certainly evolved from a kind of a hardcore based, hardcore gamer based
cues.zh: 像我这样的情况，年长玩家，在你们的游戏开发过程中是否起作用，如果是的话，你们如何应对？我得说是的。我的意思是，我自己就是个年长玩家，我认为确实有，我们肯定已经从一种硬核为基础的、硬核玩家为基础的

cues.en: industry to now we're seeing all these diverse audiences for games. And I think in a way, Civilization Revolution was kind of my response to complexative games. I think there are players that don't have 10 or 20 hours, 40 hours, 10, 15, whatever amount of time it takes to fully enjoy the fabulous Civilization PC experience. But you don't always have that.
cues.zh: 行业演变到现在我们看到各种不同的游戏受众。我认为在某种程度上，《文明革命》就是我对复杂游戏的一种回应。我认为有些玩家没有10或20小时、40小时、10、15小时，或者完全享受精彩的《文明》PC体验所需的任何时间。但你不总是有那么多时间。

cues.en: And you might want to play a game with someone who's not that deeply into civilization. So, Civil Revolution was an experience that was geared towards that audience. And it was something that I found very interesting to design. It kind of tapped into, in many ways, kind of where I was in terms of gaming. I wanted to sample a lot of different games.
cues.zh: 你可能想和没那么痴迷文明系列的人一起玩游戏。所以，《文明：革命》就是面向这类玩家的一次尝试。设计这款游戏让我觉得非常有趣。它在很多方面契合了我当时的游戏状态。我想体验很多不同的游戏。

cues.en: And so, you know, I think we're seeing this incredible diversity of games these days. I mean, from games that take only a few minutes to play, games that you play every little bit of time every day, games that you sit down with and totally devour, that take tens and tens of hours.
